Subject: RFI: Dedicated GPU Reservation (initial workbook)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this RFI. As discussed on the kickoff, AeroTech is evaluating a 12–18 month reservation for inference serving of our flight planning assistant. We need detailed answers on GPU SKUs, expected p99 latency at various batch sizes, and a recommended reservation model (mix of reserved + burst).

Attached is our RFI workbook (rfi_gpu_workbook.xlsx) with workload profiles and peak token/s request patterns. Can you fill the model rows for:

- recommended GPU SKU (best fit and cost-optimized)
- per-GPU sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for 4/8/16 sequences
- expected p50/p95/p99 latencies at specified batch sizes
- suggested reservation commit (GPUs per region) and fallback policies

We are targeting a 2000 concurrent short-session baseline with spikes to 6000 for peak launch windows. Target p99 for single-request low-latency path should be <= 350ms if possible.

Can your team return answers and the completed workbook by Thursday EOD (15 Oct)? Procurement also needs a high-level cost estimate for committed vs. on-demand.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Sanders
Head of Product AI
AeroTech AI

Appreciate the workbook and the clear SLAs. I’ve looped in Marissa (solutions lead) and Neha (enterprise sales) — they’ll drive the fill and the cost model. Quick alignment on scope:

Emma, Vivek —

Attached is the first pass: I filled the GPU profile rows and included two configuration options per workload profile. Highlights below:

- SKU suggestions:
  • High-performance: 4x A100-80GB equivalent (dense KV cache, lower quantization) — recommended for latency-critical short sessions.
  • Cost-optimized: 8x 40GB-quantized variants (aggressive int8-ish profile) — recommended for batch rerank and non-interactive workloads.

- Throughput & latency (summary):
  • For 1 request / seq len 512 (batch=1): p50 45ms / p95 120ms / p99 280–320ms (A100-80GB profile)
  • For batch=8, seq len 512: tokens/sec scales ~6.8x per GPU; p99 increases by ~1.8x vs batch=1

- Reservation recommendation:
  • Baseline reserved pool sized for 2000 concurrent short sessions (estimate: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs across two regions)
  • Burst policy: automated burst to a shared on-demand pool up to +60% with regional fallback to neighbor region, plus capacity-based throttles to maintain latency SLOs
  • Suggested commitment term: 12 months minimum with quarterly review and scaling window at 60/90/120 day marks

I’m attaching the redwood_reservation_runbook.pdf which includes autoscale knobs, recommended queueing parameters, and KV cache warm-up procedures. I also added notes in the spreadsheet on how we measured throughput (internal benchmark harness) and conservative safety margins.

Next steps: Neha to provide committed pricing bands and a quick procurement checklist. Emma — flag if we should skew more towards latency-sensitive SKUs or shift to heavier quantization.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
